title: Depot Coordinator
description:
We're looking for a highly organised and proactive Depot Coordinator to support the smooth day-to-day running of our busy operation in Lutterworth. Acting as a key link between employees, managers, agency partners, and external suppliers, you'll provide essential administrative support that helps keep our site running efficiently.

This is a varied role offering exposure to people administration, payroll support, resource planning, reporting, employee engagement, and site coordination within a fast-paced logistics environment.

Apply today and become an integral part of our Lutterworth operation.

About the Role

As Depot Coordinator, you will:
- Support employee lifecycle administration, including onboarding, job changes, absence management, and leavers.
- Complete Right to Work checks and maintain accurate employee records.
- Record and monitor attendance, holidays, sickness, overtime, and worked hours using HR and Time & Attendance systems.
- Produce daily and weekly reports relating to staffing and operational performance.
- Liaise with agency providers to coordinate labour requirements.
- Support investigations, disciplinary meetings, and employee engagement activities through note-taking and administration.
- Manage reception and visitor processes, meeting room bookings, and site communications.
- Order and control office supplies and operational consumables.
- Support resource planning and general site administration activities.

Benefits
- 23 days' annual leave
- Company Pension
- Long service rewards: both financial and leave-based.
- Health cash plan.
- Life assurance scheme.
- Critical Illness cover
- Access to our prestige benefits and rewards portal.
- Career development opportunities.
- Access to a well-established Employee Assistance Programme provider.
- And other excellent benefits you'd expect from a market leader.

Requirements

Required Knowledge & Skills

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in an administrative, depot, operations, HR, or logistics support role.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Confident communicator who can build relationships at all levels.
- Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Experience using HR, payroll, or Time & Attendance systems such as Kronos, UKG, HeRo, iTrent, or similar.
- GCSEs (or equivalent) and ideally a minimum of two years' experience in a similar role.

Additional Information
- 40 Hours per week, any 5 over 7 days
- This role supports a 24-hour operation, so flexibility around working hours may be required.
- Travel to other Whistl sites may occasionally be necessary.
- A driving licence and access to your own transport would be advantageous.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team where you can make a real impact on operational efficiency and employee experience.

title: HR Assistant
description:
HR Assistant

26-30k

Looking for your next step within HR?

This could be a great opportunity to step into a varied position where you'll work with businesses across a range of industries, helping them stay compliant and up to date with their HR documentation.

We're looking for someone with practical HR knowledge, strong communication skills and the confidence to build relationships with clients.

Day to Day
- Understanding each client's business, challenges and HR requirements.
- Advising clients on HR documentation and employment-related queries.
- Drafting bespoke HR documentation, including contracts, policies and handbooks.
- Keeping up to date with changes in employment legislation and best practice.
- Managing your own workload to meet agreed KPIs, SLAs and deadlines.
- Building strong, long-term relationships with clients through every interaction.
- Supporting existing clients with ongoing HR queries and documentation.
- Identifying opportunities to introduce relevant HR products and services.

YOU?
- Practical HR experience and a basic understanding of employment legislation.
- Someone confident communicating with clients and building rapport quickly.
- Strong written skills and attention to detail.
- A proactive, solutions-focused approach.
- The ability to research and interpret HR legislation quickly.

This is a role where you'll be trusted to take ownership, work directly with clients and develop your HR knowledge from day one.

You'll receive ongoing training and development, regular employment law updates and a clear career pathway as you progress.

If you're looking for a role where you can combine HR knowledge, client interaction and problem-solving, this could be the next step for you.

title: Part-time HR Coordinator
description:
Part-Time HR Coordinator

Castle Donington

Approx. 22 Hours Per Week (3 days) - Primarily site-based with 1 day home working, and flexible working days

Are you an organised HR professional with exceptional IT skills? Do you enjoy improving processes, managing digital systems and using technology to create efficient ways of working?

We are seeking a Part-Time HR Coordinator to join a successful and growing business based in Castle Donington. Working approximately 22 hours across 3 days per week, this role offers flexibility around which days you work, making it ideal for those seeking a better work-life balance.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who combines strong HR administration experience with a high level of IT proficiency. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining HR systems, developing digital resources, supporting onboarding processes and helping to drive improvements across HR administration and employee communications.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing the full administration process for new starters, leavers and employee changes
- Coordinating onboarding activities and preparing employment documentation
- Maintaining accurate HR records and employee data across HR systems
- Creating, developing and managing HR content within SharePoint and other digital platforms
- Supporting the implementation and continuous improvement of HR processes and systems
- Producing HR reports, metrics and management information
- Managing employee communications, policies and HR documentation
- Supporting health & safety administration and compliance activities
- Providing general HR support to employees and managers

About You

This role will suit someone who is highly organised, detail-oriented and particularly comfortable working with technology.

Essential requirements:
- Previous experience in an HR Administration, HR Assistant or HR Coordinator position
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook
- Excellent IT literacy and confidence working with HR systems and databases
- Experience creating, updating and maintaining SharePoint sites, intranet content or digital employee resources
- Comfortable learning new software and introducing more efficient ways of working
- Experience managing onboarding documentation and employee records electronically
- Strong communication and organisational skills
- Ability to handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion

What's on Offer?
- Part-time hours - approximately 22 hours per week
- 3 days per week with flexibility on working days
- Hybrid working with up to 1 day per week from home
- Varied and interesting HR role with broad responsibility
- Opportunity to make a real impact through process and system improvements
- Friendly and supportive working environment

This role is ideal for a HR professional who enjoys both the people and systems side of HR. If you're highly IT literate, enjoy building digital solutions such as SharePoint resources, and take pride in creating efficient HR processes, we'd love to hear from you.

Should you require any support or assistance, please contact your local Gi Group office.

title: People Services (HR) Assistant
company: Leicestershire Fire and Rescue - Agency - Contract
description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service as a People Services Assistant on a fixed-term maternity cover contract.

You will be a key member of a small People Services Team, working across many aspects of People Services, including recruitment, contracts, and payroll administration, as well as providing administrative support (including note taking) to the People Partner team during employee relations cases.

You will need to be able to think fast and be confident working in a busy environment, dealing with high demand from our internal customers, and be able to provide a high level of customer service.

We re looking for a level-headed, enthusiastic, and proactive individual, preferably with administrative experience and an interest in People Services (HR). You ll need to have excellent communication skills and great attention to detail, with a right first-time approach to support the delivery of a high-quality People Service.

In addition, you will be required to travel to Service locations to complete disclosure and barring service checks and engage and foster good relations with the wider workforce.

This is a challenging and immensely rewarding position. If you ve got what it takes, we want you to join us. This is a great opportunity to work in People Services and will suit individuals looking for a sideways move, or seeking to enter People Services for the first time.

Benefits you will receive:
- Competitive salary
- Flexible working
- Generous leave entitlement plus public holidays
- Full support for ongoing professional development
- On-site gym facilities
- Free onsite parking
- Access to an emergency services Blue Light discount card
- Use of our in-house occupational health unit, which includes fitness support
- Access to the Service s 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
- Public sector pension (subject to pension scheme rules). You will automatically be enrolled into the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS), which is a tax-approved, defined-benefit occupational pension scheme. Your contributions are based on your earnings, and you can choose from different income options when you retire.

Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service is committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion in the workplace. Furthermore, we want to create a work environment where everyone feels safe, can be themselves and can perform their roles to the best of their abilities. We have signed up with a number of nationally recognised organisations that promote equality, diversity and inclusion and we are working with them to help us achieve our objectives. These organisations include:
- Employers Network for Equality and Inclusion
- Department of Works and Pension s Disability Confident scheme
- Asian Fire Service Association (AFSA)

Safer Recruitment

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people, and vulnerable adults. Safer recruitment practices, including identity, reference, and appropriate criminal record checks, will be applied throughout the recruitment process.

Pension Considerations

Please note that it is your personal responsibility to check whether by applying/accepting this position it would result in any Annual Allowance or Lifetime Allowance implications. A breach in the Annual Allowance threshold could result in a Tax charge. A breach in the Lifetime Allowance threshold will result in a Tax charge. Further information on Annual Allowance and Lifetime Allowance can be obtained from our Pensions team.

Sponsorship

Please take note that Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service does not hold a UK Visa & Immigration (UKVI) Skilled Worker License sponsor and are unable to sponsor any individuals for Skilled Worker Sponsorship.

Closing date: 23: October 2026

Interview and test date: W/C 9 November 2026

If you are invited to interview, you will be assessed against the NFCC Leadership Framework. The highest level relevant to the role is outlined in the person specification for the position you are applying for. The interview may include both behavioural and role-specific questions to assess your suitability. You will also be asked a question exploring your understanding of, and commitment to, Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) in the workplace.

Internal Candidates

If the successful candidate is a current employee within LFRS, the terms of the appointment will be agreed with management, in consultation with the People Team.

Job Objectives
- To undertake processes and procedures to ensure the effective delivery of People Services
- Provide advice to managers, employees and the wider People Team on the broad range of People Services topics
- Manage and progress all aspects of transactional People Services relating to the employee lifecycle, utilising relevant Human Resource Information Systems

Skills Required
- Experience of delivering exceptional customer service
- Competent in a range of Microsoft Office software
- Ability to work in a pressurised environment, where priorities can change
- Experience of taking minutes or note taking using a computer during meetings
- Ability to communicate at all levels including Senior Management

title: Recruitment Resourcer
description:
Ideal recruit are looking for a Recruitment Resourcer to join our growing Industrial team in Leicester, supporting our clients and their operations.

This is a great opportunity to become part of a supportive team where you ll play a key role in helping clients find the right people for their warehouse operations.

What you ll be doing:
- Working closely with management to understand recruitment needs and client requirements
- Supporting our clients by delivering a high-quality recruitment service
- Sourcing candidates using a range of tools (CV databases, job boards, open days, etc.)
- Managing the full recruitment process, from initial contact through to onboarding
- Registering new candidates and ensuring all compliance is up to date
- Supporting the team with general recruitment administration

What we re looking for:
- A motivated and reliable individual with a positive attitude
- Someone proactive, organised, and responsive
- Ability to manage a busy workload and prioritise tasks effectively
- Willingness to learn and grow within a developing company

What we offer:
- Full-time
- Salary £25.842 - depending on experience
- Monday to Friday, 09 00
- Full training and resources provided to support your development

Requirements:
- Previous recruitment experience is desirable (minimum 6 months), but not essential
- Driving licence is required

If this sounds like a role for you, please apply with your up-to-date CV - we d love to hear from you!

Leicester

- Telephone screening candidate calls.
- Meeting candidates face to face to obtain identification.

- Building strong candidate relationships.
- Working towards recruitment targets and deadlines.

About You:
- Friendly, confident and professional.
- A strong communicator with good telephone skills.
- Organised and able to multitask.
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.
- Confident using computers and Microsoft Office.

What We Offer:
- Full Training and coaching.
- Opportunities to develop your recruitment career.
- A friendly working environment.
- Modern office with free car parking.
